faq.q: How much does iAccident Lawyer charge?
faq.a: iAccident Lawyer publishes a contingency fee, which means the fee is a share of what the case recovers and there is nothing to pay if it recovers nothing. The rate itself is not published, so ask for it in writing, along with how case expenses are handled and whether they come out of the recovery before or after the fee. The first consultation is free, which is the place to ask.

faq.q: Does iAccident Lawyer offer a free consultation?
faq.a: Yes. iAccident Lawyer publishes a free initial consultation. The intake line is published as open around the clock and the firm states it will visit clients in hospital or at home.

faq.q: Where does iAccident Lawyer have offices?
faq.a: iAccident Lawyer publishes 13 offices, among them Los Angeles, Newport Beach, Huntington Beach and Anaheim. Addresses and the Google listing behind each one are on this profile under Offices.

faq.q: Who are the attorneys at iAccident Lawyer?
faq.a: iAccident Lawyer names one attorney on its own site, and each is listed on this profile with the page we read them from. They have not been checked against a state register: California does not publish an attorney register we can query, so licensure is not verified here. The state's own attorney search is the place to check it.

Could not be answered from any public source and therefore counts neither for nor against the firm: licensure, discipline and entity registration.
